title: Reduce GPU memory: activation checkpointing, scratch buffers, and arena tuning
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: Recent production workloads and perf canaries showed higher-than-expected GPU memory footprints for long-context generation and high-concurrency serving. This PR reduces peak GPU memory and transient workspace usage by combining three complementary changes: (1) make activation checkpointing opportunistic and less conservative (reduce saved activations for attention blocks when safe), (2) cap and reuse scratch buffers more aggressively via a bucketed allocator, and (3) tune the arena allocator heuristics to favor smaller persistent arenas and more fragmented-but-recyclable arenas for short-lived kernel workspaces. Together these changes reduce end-to-end GPU memory usage for representative models (Llama-2/Redwood-13B/Redwood-70B variants) by 5-12% depending on sequence length and batch shape. Changes in this PR are opt-in behind runtime flags and default-on for hosted fast-paths after a staged rollout.

What changed (high level): 
- Activation checkpointing: added a new policy layer that marks certain attention/FFN subgraphs as "safely-checkpointable" based on analytics and operator characteristics; default checkpointing granularity reduced from block-level to half-block for selected layers to limit activation retention. Implemented a runtime flag runtime.gpu.activation_checkpointing.policy with values conservative|balanced|aggressive. 
- Scratch buffers: introduced a compacting bucketed scratch allocator (runtime/gpu/allocator/scratch_allocator.*) which reuses transient buffers across op invocations and enforces per-stream caps. Added logic to request smaller scratch ranges for fused attention kernels when KV-cache is present. 
- Arena tuning: adjusted arena size growth policy and introduced an eviction heuristic that moves small-unused arenas to a per-device recycle list instead of holding a single large arena; changed default arena max to favor many smaller arenas for mixed-length workloads. 
- KV-cache interaction: when KV-cache is enabled we reduce ephemeral workspace allocation (scratch) and prefer in-place KV operations, lowering temporary memory spikes. 
- Scheduler/batching: added a small safeguard in the continuous-batcher to avoid coalescing large-variable-length requests that would blow up per-batch workspace. This is conservative and opt-in via continuous_batcher.max_workspace_ratio. 
- Tests and telemetry: added microbenchmarks, system perf tests, and new metrics (gpu.arena.used_bytes, gpu.scratch.reuse_rate, gpu.activation.checkpointed_layers) and dashboards.

Backward-compatibility / rollout: defaults are set to balanced to preserve latency/SLOs. The change is gated so Dedicated/private customers can opt-out. We plan a staged rollout: canary (hosted, low-traffic), regional rollout, and then global default.

Notes: All description text is in this single continuous string as requested.

release_notes: Reduced GPU peak and transient workspace memory via opportunistic activation checkpointing, bucketed scratch buffer reuse, and tuned arena allocator heuristics. Expected 5-12% GPU memory reduction on long-context and high-concurrency workloads with minimal p99 latency impact under the default 'balanced' policy. Rollout is staged and configurable via runtime flags (runtime.gpu.activation_checkpointing.policy, continuous_batcher.max_workspace_ratio).
